approved_indications: Intestinal nematode infestations (Ascaris lumbricoides, Enterobius, Hookworm); Neurocysticercosis and hydatid cyst disease; Amoebiasis, giardiasis, and anaerobic intra-abdominal and dental infections (Metronidazole); Plasmodium falciparum and vivax malaria treatment (Artemisinin combination therapy)
reference_dosage: Intestinal deworming: Albendazole 400 mg as a single chewable dose; Amoebiasis: Metronidazole 400–800 mg 3 times daily for 7–10 days.
serious_adverse_effects: Severe Disulfiram-like reaction (severe vomiting, tachycardia, flushing) if alcohol is consumed with Metronidazole
Peripheral neuropathy and encephalopathy with prolonged Metronidazole therapy
Bone marrow suppression and transaminase elevations with prolonged Albendazole
contraindications: First trimester of pregnancy (Albendazole possesses embryotoxic/teratogenic potential)
Severe active liver disease
Alcohol consumption during Metronidazole and for 48h after
drug_interactions: Alcohol: Extreme disulfiram-like ethanol intolerance reaction with Nitroimidazoles
Warfarin: Metronidazole inhibits CYP2C9, markedly increasing anticoagulant effect and bleeding risk

approved_indications: Vitamin D deficiency, nutritional rickets, and osteomalacia / osteoporosis prophylaxis; Peripheral neuropathy, diabetic neuropathy, and vitamin B12 deficiency anemia; Iron deficiency anemia and nutritional prophylaxis during pregnancy and lactation; Neural tube defect prevention (Preconceptional Folic Acid supplementation)
reference_dosage: Cholecalciferol: 60,000 IU once weekly for 8 weeks, followed by once monthly maintenance; Calcium: 500–1000 mg daily post-meals; Methylcobalamin: 1500 mcg daily.
common_side_effects: Constipation, dark tarry stools, and nausea (Iron supplements)
serious_adverse_effects: Hypercalcemia, metastatic tissue calcification, and renal calculi (Vitamin D / Calcium toxicity)
Iron overload / hemochromatosis in non-iron deficiency states
contraindications: Hypercalcemia, hypervitaminosis D, or severe nephrolithiasis
Hemochromatosis, hemosiderosis, or active hemolytic anemia (for iron supplements)
drug_interactions: Iron and Calcium bind and inactivate Fluoroquinolones and Tetracyclines (separate by 2–3 hours)
Thiazide diuretics increase hypercalcemia risk when co-administered with high-dose calcium/vitamin D

Concurrent live attenuated vaccines

Ketoconazole: Inhibits steroid metabolism, heightening toxicity

Fluid retention and facial mooning (Cushingoid features)

Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT)

serious_adverse_effects: Dose-dependent acute hepatic necrosis (N-acetyl-p-benzoquinone imine hepatotoxicity)
Renal tubular necrosis
Thrombocytopenia or leukopenia
contraindications: Severe active hepatic impairment or acute viral hepatitis
Documented hypersensitivity to paracetamol
drug_interactions: Chronic heavy alcohol intake markedly potentiates hepatotoxic risk
Warfarin: Regular high doses (>2g/day) may elevate INR
Isoniazid (elevates hepatotoxic metabolite formation)

approved_indications: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy and post-herpetic neuralgia; Focal and generalized tonic-clonic epileptic seizures; Trigeminal neuralgia (Carbamazepine first-line); Fibromyalgia and chronic neuropathic radiculopathy
reference_dosage: Pregabalin: 75 mg twice daily, titrating to 150 mg twice daily; Levetiracetam: 500 mg twice daily, titrating up to 1,500 mg twice daily.
serious_adverse_effects: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (DRESS, SJS/TEN)
Suicidal ideation and behavioral changes (aggression, agitation with levetiracetam)
Hepatic necrosis and pancreatitis (Sodium Valproate)
Aplastic anemia and agranulocytosis (Carbamazepine)
contraindications: Valproate is strictly contraindicated in women of childbearing potential unless pregnancy prevention program in place (severe teratogenicity)
Atrioventricular heart block (Carbamazepine)
drug_interactions: Central nervous system depressants (additive sedation)
Combined oral contraceptives (hepatic enzyme inducers reduce contraceptive efficacy)
Warfarin (enzyme inducers reduce anticoagulant levels)

reference_dosage: Vaginal candidiasis: 150 mg as a single oral dose; Onychomycosis: Terbinafine 250 mg once daily for 6–12 weeks; Itraconazole: 100–200 mg twice daily with food.
serious_adverse_effects: Drug-induced hepatotoxicity and fatal acute liver failure

Congestive heart failure exacerbation (Itraconazole negative inotropic warning)
Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (TEN/SJS)

Ventricular dysfunction or heart failure (for Itraconazole)

PPIs/H2-blockers: Reduce gastric acid and severely impair Itraconazole capsule absorption

reference_dosage: Salbutamol MDI: 1–2 puffs (100–200 mcg) as needed for acute relief (max 8 puffs/24h); Budesonide: 200–400 mcg inhaled twice daily.
serious_adverse_effects: Paradoxical bronchospasm
Hypokalemia at high doses
Cardiac arrhythmias
Adrenal axis suppression with prolonged high-dose ICS
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to salbutamol or inhaled corticosteroid formulations
Severe milk protein allergy (for dry powder inhalers containing lactose)
drug_interactions: Non-selective Beta-blockers (propranolol) severely antagonize bronchodilation and trigger bronchospasm
Potassium-depleting diuretics (enhance hypokalemia risk)

serious_adverse_effects: Lactic acidosis (rare but fatal with Metformin in severe hypoxia/renal failure)
Severe neuroglycopenic hypoglycemia
Euglycemic Diabetic Ketoacidosis (SGLT-2i)
Acute pancreatitis (DPP-4i)
contraindications: Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min for Metformin/SGLT2i)
Acute metabolic acidosis, DKA, or diabetic coma
Severe hepatic failure
drug_interactions: Iodinated Radiocontrast agents (withhold Metformin 48h prior/after)
Systemic corticosteroids (antagonize glycemic control)
Beta-blockers (mask adrenergic hypoglycemia warning signs)

approved_indications: Vitamin D deficiency, nutritional rickets, and osteomalacia / osteoporosis prophylaxis; Peripheral neuropathy, diabetic neuropathy, and vitamin B12 deficiency anemia; Iron deficiency anemia and nutritional prophylaxis during pregnancy and lactation; Neural tube defect prevention (Preconceptional Folic Acid supplementation)
reference_dosage: Cholecalciferol: 60,000 IU once weekly for 8 weeks, followed by once monthly maintenance; Calcium: 500–1000 mg daily post-meals; Methylcobalamin: 1500 mcg daily.
common_side_effects: Constipation, dark tarry stools, and nausea (Iron supplements)
serious_adverse_effects: Hypercalcemia, metastatic tissue calcification, and renal calculi (Vitamin D / Calcium toxicity)
Iron overload / hemochromatosis in non-iron deficiency states
contraindications: Hypercalcemia, hypervitaminosis D, or severe nephrolithiasis
Hemochromatosis, hemosiderosis, or active hemolytic anemia (for iron supplements)
drug_interactions: Iron and Calcium bind and inactivate Fluoroquinolones and Tetracyclines (separate by 2–3 hours)
Thiazide diuretics increase hypercalcemia risk when co-administered with high-dose calcium/vitamin D

approved_indications: Pyrexia (fever) secondary to infectious, inflammatory, or post-vaccination etiology; Mild-to-moderate somatic pain (headache, tension headache, migraine attack); Musculoskeletal discomfort, backache, arthralgia, and dental pain; Primary dysmenorrhea and post-procedural discomfort
reference_dosage: Adults: 500 mg–650 mg orally every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Maximum daily dose MUST NOT exceed 4,000 mg (4g) in 24 hours.
serious_adverse_effects: Dose-dependent acute hepatic necrosis (N-acetyl-p-benzoquinone imine hepatotoxicity)
Renal tubular necrosis
Thrombocytopenia or leukopenia
contraindications: Severe active hepatic impairment or acute viral hepatitis
Documented hypersensitivity to paracetamol
drug_interactions: Chronic heavy alcohol intake markedly potentiates hepatotoxic risk
Warfarin: Regular high doses (>2g/day) may elevate INR
Isoniazid (elevates hepatotoxic metabolite formation)

approved_indications: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and erosive esophagitis; Peptic and duodenal ulcer healing and maintenance therapy; Zollinger-Ellison syndrome and gastric hypersecretory states; NSAID-associated mucosal ulcer prophylaxis and H. pylori eradication protocols
reference_dosage: Adults: 40 mg orally once daily 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast for 4–8 weeks. Intravenous: 40 mg IV slow bolus.
serious_adverse_effects: Long-term hypomagnesemia and vitamin B12 malabsorption
Increased incidence of Clostridioides difficile colitis
Elevated risk of osteoporotic hip fractures with multi-year high-dose therapy
Acute interstitial nephritis
contraindications: Known severe hypersensitivity to pantoprazole, substituted benzimidazoles, or excipients
drug_interactions: Clopidogrel: Some PPIs (omeprazole) may reduce antiplatelet bioactivation; prefer pantoprazole
Iron supplements, Ketoconazole (reduced bioavailability due to elevated gastric pH)
Methotrexate (PPIs may delay clearance, increasing toxicity)

approved_indications: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy and post-herpetic neuralgia; Focal and generalized tonic-clonic epileptic seizures; Trigeminal neuralgia (Carbamazepine first-line); Fibromyalgia and chronic neuropathic radiculopathy
reference_dosage: Pregabalin: 75 mg twice daily, titrating to 150 mg twice daily; Levetiracetam: 500 mg twice daily, titrating up to 1,500 mg twice daily.
serious_adverse_effects: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (DRESS, SJS/TEN)
Suicidal ideation and behavioral changes (aggression, agitation with levetiracetam)
Hepatic necrosis and pancreatitis (Sodium Valproate)
Aplastic anemia and agranulocytosis (Carbamazepine)
contraindications: Valproate is strictly contraindicated in women of childbearing potential unless pregnancy prevention program in place (severe teratogenicity)
Atrioventricular heart block (Carbamazepine)
drug_interactions: Central nervous system depressants (additive sedation)
Combined oral contraceptives (hepatic enzyme inducers reduce contraceptive efficacy)
Warfarin (enzyme inducers reduce anticoagulant levels)

approved_indications: Severe acute bronchial asthma exacerbation and COPD status asthmaticus; Systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, and acute vasculitis flares; Severe allergic angioedema, anaphylaxis adjunctive therapy, and drug eruptions; Nephrotic syndrome and immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP)
reference_dosage: Prednisolone: 20–40 mg once daily morning for 5–7 days for acute asthma; taper gradually if treatment exceeds 2 weeks to avoid secondary adrenal crisis.
common_side_effects: Increased appetite and rapid weight gain
Fluid retention and facial mooning (Cushingoid features)
serious_adverse_effects: Secondary hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis suppression and adrenal crisis upon abrupt cessation
Hyperglycemia and steroid-induced diabetes
Opportunistic systemic infections and reactivation of latent tuberculosis
Avascular necrosis of the femoral head and severe osteoporosis
Posterior subcapsular cataracts and open-angle glaucoma
contraindications: Systemic untreated fungal or parasitic infections
Active untreated tuberculosis or viral infections (herpes simplex keratitis)
Concurrent live attenuated vaccines
drug_interactions: NSAIDs: Markedly increases risk of severe peptic ulceration and catastrophic GI bleeding
Antidiabetic medications: Corticosteroids elevate blood glucose, necessitating higher antidiabetic doses
Ketoconazole: Inhibits steroid metabolism, heightening toxicity

approved_indications: Secondary prevention of atherothrombotic events post-STEMI / NSTEMI / stroke; Non-valvular atrial fibrillation for systemic thromboembolism / stroke prevention; Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) treatment and prophylaxis; Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT)
reference_dosage: Ecosprin: 75–150 mg once daily post-meal; Clopidogrel: 75 mg once daily; Apixaban: 5 mg twice daily. Strictly per cardiology guidelines.
serious_adverse_effects: Major gastrointestinal bleeding
Intracranial hemorrhage and hemorrhagic stroke
Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT)
contraindications: Active pathological bleeding (peptic ulcer, intracranial bleed)
Severe thrombocytopenia (<50,000/uL)
Severe uncontrolled arterial hypertension (>180/110 mmHg)
drug_interactions: NSAIDs and Corticosteroids (substantially amplify GI ulceration and major bleeding risk)
CYP2C19 inhibitors (Omeprazole impairs Clopidogrel bioactivation; use Pantoprazole)
SSRIs (additive bleeding risk)

approved_indications: Prescription medical management corresponding to therapeutic class 'Gastrointestinal medicines'.; Conditions diagnosed and evaluated by a licensed medical practitioner.
reference_dosage: General Reference: Dosage is strictly clinical and depends upon individual age, weight, hepatic/renal clearance, and disease severity. Strictly consult your prescribing doctor.
serious_adverse_effects: Severe allergic hypersensitivity (rash, facial swelling, breathing difficulty)
Unusual bleeding, unexplained bruising, or severe persistent dizziness
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to active pharmaceutical ingredients or excipients
Severe hepatic or renal insufficiency unless evaluated by a clinician
drug_interactions: Concurrent prescription medications, anticoagulants, or OTC supplements may interact. Inform your physician of all concurrent regimens.

approved_indications: Adjuvant endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive early breast cancer in postmenopausal women; Advanced and metastatic hormone receptor-positive breast cancer; Reduction of febrile neutropenia duration in cytotoxic chemotherapy (Filgrastim); Bone metastases hypercalcemia and skeletal-related event prevention (Zoledronic Acid)
reference_dosage: Letrozole: 2.5 mg once daily continuously for 5 years; Filgrastim: 5 mcg/kg/day SC starting 24h after cytotoxic chemotherapy until ANC recovery.
common_side_effects: Arthralgia, bone pain, and joint stiffness
serious_adverse_effects: Severe bone mineral density loss and accelerated osteoporotic fractures
Thromboembolic events (deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism with Tamoxifen)
Splenic rupture (rare with Filgrastim)
Osteonecrosis of the jaw (Zoledronic Acid)
contraindications: Premenopausal endocrine status (for aromatase inhibitors without ovarian suppression)
Pregnancy and breastfeeding (severe teratogenic and fetal toxicity warning)
Severe hepatic impairment
drug_interactions: Tamoxifen with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (Fluoxetine, Paroxetine) prevents bioactivation into endoxifen, reducing anticancer efficacy; prefer Venlafaxine
Warfarin (Tamoxifen significantly potentiates anticoagulant effect)
schedule: Schedule H Prescription Drug / Oncology Formulary

approved_indications: Vaginal candidiasis (acute and recurrent episodes); Oropharyngeal and esophageal candidiasis in immunocompromised hosts; Tinea corporis, tinea cruris, tinea pedis, and onychomycosis (fungal nail infection); Cryptococcal meningitis and systemic endemic mycoses
reference_dosage: Vaginal candidiasis: 150 mg as a single oral dose; Onychomycosis: Terbinafine 250 mg once daily for 6–12 weeks; Itraconazole: 100–200 mg twice daily with food.

Neuropsychiatric events and delirium (Oseltamivir in adolescents)
contraindications: Known severe hypersensitivity to acyclovir, valacyclovir, or oseltamivir
drug_interactions: Probenecid: Competitively inhibits renal clearance, increasing antiviral blood levels
Nephrotoxic agents (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides): Greatly increase acute renal failure risk

approved_indications: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) lower urinary tract symptoms (hesitancy, weak stream, nocturia); Medical expulsion therapy for distal ureteral calculi (<10 mm); Overactive bladder syndrome with urinary urgency and urge incontinence (Solifenacin/Mirabegron)
reference_dosage: Tamsulosin: 0.4 mg once daily taken approximately 30 minutes after the same meal each day; Finasteride: 5 mg once daily.
common_side_effects: Retrograde ejaculation or decreased ejaculatory volume
serious_adverse_effects: Intraoperative Floppy Iris Syndrome (IFIS) during cataract surgery
Severe orthostatic hypotension and syncope
Severe allergic angioedema
contraindications: History of orthostatic hypotension or syncope
Severe hepatic insufficiency (Child-Pugh Class C)
Pregnant women must not handle broken or crushed 5-ARI tablets (causes male fetal pseudohermaphroditism)
drug_interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (Ketoconazole) and PDE-5 inhibitors (Sildenafil) cause additive vasodilation and severe hypotension
Antihypertensives (monitor for postural dizziness)

approved_indications: Severe acute bronchial asthma exacerbation and COPD status asthmaticus; Systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, and acute vasculitis flares; Severe allergic angioedema, anaphylaxis adjunctive therapy, and drug eruptions; Nephrotic syndrome and immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP)
reference_dosage: Prednisolone: 20–40 mg once daily morning for 5–7 days for acute asthma; taper gradually if treatment exceeds 2 weeks to avoid secondary adrenal crisis.
common_side_effects: Increased appetite and rapid weight gain
Fluid retention and facial mooning (Cushingoid features)
serious_adverse_effects: Secondary hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis suppression and adrenal crisis upon abrupt cessation
Hyperglycemia and steroid-induced diabetes
Opportunistic systemic infections and reactivation of latent tuberculosis
Avascular necrosis of the femoral head and severe osteoporosis
Posterior subcapsular cataracts and open-angle glaucoma
contraindications: Systemic untreated fungal or parasitic infections
Active untreated tuberculosis or viral infections (herpes simplex keratitis)
Concurrent live attenuated vaccines
drug_interactions: NSAIDs: Markedly increases risk of severe peptic ulceration and catastrophic GI bleeding
Antidiabetic medications: Corticosteroids elevate blood glucose, necessitating higher antidiabetic doses
Ketoconazole: Inhibits steroid metabolism, heightening toxicity

approved_indications: Secondary prevention of atherothrombotic events post-STEMI / NSTEMI / stroke; Non-valvular atrial fibrillation for systemic thromboembolism / stroke prevention; Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) treatment and prophylaxis; Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT)
reference_dosage: Ecosprin: 75–150 mg once daily post-meal; Clopidogrel: 75 mg once daily; Apixaban: 5 mg twice daily. Strictly per cardiology guidelines.
serious_adverse_effects: Major gastrointestinal bleeding
Intracranial hemorrhage and hemorrhagic stroke
Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT)
contraindications: Active pathological bleeding (peptic ulcer, intracranial bleed)
Severe thrombocytopenia (<50,000/uL)
Severe uncontrolled arterial hypertension (>180/110 mmHg)
drug_interactions: NSAIDs and Corticosteroids (substantially amplify GI ulceration and major bleeding risk)
CYP2C19 inhibitors (Omeprazole impairs Clopidogrel bioactivation; use Pantoprazole)
SSRIs (additive bleeding risk)

approved_indications: Adjuvant endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive early breast cancer in postmenopausal women; Advanced and metastatic hormone receptor-positive breast cancer; Reduction of febrile neutropenia duration in cytotoxic chemotherapy (Filgrastim); Bone metastases hypercalcemia and skeletal-related event prevention (Zoledronic Acid)
reference_dosage: Letrozole: 2.5 mg once daily continuously for 5 years; Filgrastim: 5 mcg/kg/day SC starting 24h after cytotoxic chemotherapy until ANC recovery.
common_side_effects: Arthralgia, bone pain, and joint stiffness
serious_adverse_effects: Severe bone mineral density loss and accelerated osteoporotic fractures
Thromboembolic events (deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism with Tamoxifen)
Splenic rupture (rare with Filgrastim)
Osteonecrosis of the jaw (Zoledronic Acid)
contraindications: Premenopausal endocrine status (for aromatase inhibitors without ovarian suppression)
Pregnancy and breastfeeding (severe teratogenic and fetal toxicity warning)
Severe hepatic impairment
drug_interactions: Tamoxifen with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (Fluoxetine, Paroxetine) prevents bioactivation into endoxifen, reducing anticancer efficacy; prefer Venlafaxine
Warfarin (Tamoxifen significantly potentiates anticoagulant effect)
schedule: Schedule H Prescription Drug / Oncology Formulary

approved_indications: Essential systemic hypertension in adults; Cardiovascular risk reduction in diabetic and coronary artery disease patients; Stable chronic angina pectoris and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction; Diabetic nephropathy with microalbuminuria
reference_dosage: Telmisartan: 40–80 mg once daily; Amlodipine: 5–10 mg once daily; Metoprolol: 25–50 mg twice daily. Titrate according to clinical BP targets.
serious_adverse_effects: Symptomatic hypotension and syncope
Hyperkalemia (ARBs, ACEi, Spironolactone)
Severe bradycardia or heart block (Beta-blockers)
Angioedema
contraindications: Pregnancy (ARBs & ACE inhibitors carry fatal fetotoxicity warning)
Bilateral renal artery stenosis
Severe cardiogenic shock or 2nd/3rd degree AV block (Beta-blockers)
drug_interactions: Potassium supplements/Potassium-sparing diuretics (severe hyperkalemia risk)
NSAIDs (blunt BP reduction and increase renal failure risk)
Phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors (excessive hypotension)

approved_indications: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and erosive esophagitis; Peptic and duodenal ulcer healing and maintenance therapy; Zollinger-Ellison syndrome and gastric hypersecretory states; NSAID-associated mucosal ulcer prophylaxis and H. pylori eradication protocols
reference_dosage: Adults: 40 mg orally once daily 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast for 4–8 weeks. Intravenous: 40 mg IV slow bolus.
serious_adverse_effects: Long-term hypomagnesemia and vitamin B12 malabsorption
Increased incidence of Clostridioides difficile colitis
Elevated risk of osteoporotic hip fractures with multi-year high-dose therapy
Acute interstitial nephritis
contraindications: Known severe hypersensitivity to pantoprazole, substituted benzimidazoles, or excipients
drug_interactions: Clopidogrel: Some PPIs (omeprazole) may reduce antiplatelet bioactivation; prefer pantoprazole
Iron supplements, Ketoconazole (reduced bioavailability due to elevated gastric pH)
Methotrexate (PPIs may delay clearance, increasing toxicity)

approved_indications: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus as monotherapy or combination pharmacotherapy; Cardiovascular and renal risk reduction in T2DM patients (SGLT-2 inhibitors); Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus and gestational diabetes (Insulin regimens)
reference_dosage: Metformin: 500 mg twice daily with meals, titrating up to 2,000 mg daily; Glimepiride: 1–2 mg once daily before breakfast.
serious_adverse_effects: Lactic acidosis (rare but fatal with Metformin in severe hypoxia/renal failure)
Severe neuroglycopenic hypoglycemia
Euglycemic Diabetic Ketoacidosis (SGLT-2i)
Acute pancreatitis (DPP-4i)
contraindications: Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min for Metformin/SGLT2i)
Acute metabolic acidosis, DKA, or diabetic coma
Severe hepatic failure
drug_interactions: Iodinated Radiocontrast agents (withhold Metformin 48h prior/after)
Systemic corticosteroids (antagonize glycemic control)

approved_indications: Infiltration anesthesia and peripheral nerve block for minor surgical and dental procedures; Surface topical anesthesia for endotracheal intubation, endoscopy, and urethral catheterization; Spinal and epidural anesthesia for obstetrical and lower abdominal / orthopedic surgery; Induction and maintenance of general anesthesia in procedural sedation (Propofol/Midazolam)
reference_dosage: Lignocaine 2% plain: Maximum single dose is 4.5 mg/kg body weight (not exceeding 300 mg); Lignocaine with adrenaline: Max 7 mg/kg (up to 500 mg). Strictly individualized.
common_side_effects: Mild localized burning or stinging during injection
Transient numbness and paresthesia in adjacent dermatomes
Mild hypotension upon spinal sympathetic blockade
serious_adverse_effects: Local Anesthetic Systemic Toxicity (LAST): Perioral numbness, metallic taste, auditory tinnitus, seizures, and cardiovascular collapse
Severe bupivacaine-induced refractory cardiac arrest and ventricular arrhythmias
Malignant hyperthermia and severe respiratory depression
contraindications: Severe cardiac conduction blocks (2nd or 3rd degree AV block without pacemaker)
Known hypersensitivity to amide-type local anesthetics
Injection into infected or acutely inflamed tissue (acidic pH prevents active drug penetration)
drug_interactions: Class I and III antiarrhythmics (additive cardiac electrophysiological depression)
Adrenaline-containing solutions MUST NOT be used for digital, penile, nasal, or ear-lobe block (causes severe ischemic necrosis)
schedule: Schedule H Prescription Drug / Controlled Hospital Anesthetic

approved_indications: Vitamin D deficiency, nutritional rickets, and osteomalacia / osteoporosis prophylaxis; Peripheral neuropathy, diabetic neuropathy, and vitamin B12 deficiency anemia; Iron deficiency anemia and nutritional prophylaxis during pregnancy and lactation; Neural tube defect prevention (Preconceptional Folic Acid supplementation)
reference_dosage: Cholecalciferol: 60,000 IU once weekly for 8 weeks, followed by once monthly maintenance; Calcium: 500–1000 mg daily post-meals; Methylcobalamin: 1500 mcg daily.
common_side_effects: Constipation, dark tarry stools, and nausea (Iron supplements)
serious_adverse_effects: Hypercalcemia, metastatic tissue calcification, and renal calculi (Vitamin D / Calcium toxicity)
Iron overload / hemochromatosis in non-iron deficiency states
contraindications: Hypercalcemia, hypervitaminosis D, or severe nephrolithiasis
Hemochromatosis, hemosiderosis, or active hemolytic anemia (for iron supplements)
drug_interactions: Iron and Calcium bind and inactivate Fluoroquinolones and Tetracyclines (separate by 2–3 hours)
Thiazide diuretics increase hypercalcemia risk when co-administered with high-dose calcium/vitamin D

approved_indications: Abnormal uterine bleeding (menorrhagia) and dysfunctional uterine bleeding; Luteal phase support in assisted reproductive technology (ART) and recurrent miscarriage prophylaxis; Endometriosis, secondary amenorrhea, and post-menopausal hormone therapy adjunct; Post-partum hemorrhage prevention and management (Tranexamic Acid / Oxytocin)
reference_dosage: Tranexamic Acid: 500 mg–1000 mg orally 3 times daily during active heavy menstrual flow; Dydrogesterone: 10 mg 1–2 times daily from cycle day 11 to 25.
serious_adverse_effects: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism, and retinal vein thrombosis (Tranexamic Acid in prothrombotic states)
Severe cholestatic jaundice and hepatic impairment
Visual disturbances or color blindness (Tranexamic Acid)
contraindications: Active thromboembolic disease or history of venous/arterial thrombosis
Known or suspected estrogen/progesterone-dependent malignancy (breast or endometrial cancer)
Undiagnosed abnormal genital bleeding
Severe renal impairment (Tranexamic Acid requires strict dose reduction)
drug_interactions: Combined Oral Contraceptives: Concurrent use with Tranexamic Acid markedly elevates thrombotic risk
Anticoagulants: Antagonistic or complex clotting interactions

Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT)

approved_indications: Severe acute bronchial asthma exacerbation and COPD status asthmaticus; Systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, and acute vasculitis flares; Severe allergic angioedema, anaphylaxis adjunctive therapy, and drug eruptions; Nephrotic syndrome and immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP)

common_side_effects: Increased appetite and rapid weight gain
Fluid retention and facial mooning (Cushingoid features)

Opportunistic systemic infections and reactivation of latent tuberculosis
Avascular necrosis of the femoral head and severe osteoporosis
Posterior subcapsular cataracts and open-angle glaucoma

Active untreated tuberculosis or viral infections (herpes simplex keratitis)
Concurrent live attenuated vaccines

Ketoconazole: Inhibits steroid metabolism, heightening toxicity

approved_indications: Abnormal uterine bleeding (menorrhagia) and dysfunctional uterine bleeding; Luteal phase support in assisted reproductive technology (ART) and recurrent miscarriage prophylaxis; Endometriosis, secondary amenorrhea, and post-menopausal hormone therapy adjunct; Post-partum hemorrhage prevention and management (Tranexamic Acid / Oxytocin)
reference_dosage: Tranexamic Acid: 500 mg–1000 mg orally 3 times daily during active heavy menstrual flow; Dydrogesterone: 10 mg 1–2 times daily from cycle day 11 to 25.

Known or suspected estrogen/progesterone-dependent malignancy (breast or endometrial cancer)
Undiagnosed abnormal genital bleeding
Severe renal impairment (Tranexamic Acid requires strict dose reduction)
drug_interactions: Combined Oral Contraceptives: Concurrent use with Tranexamic Acid markedly elevates thrombotic risk
Anticoagulants: Antagonistic or complex clotting interactions

approved_indications: Active immunization against Clostridium tetani following trauma or wound contamination; Post-exposure rabies prophylaxis following animal bites or scratches (WHO Category II & III); Annual seasonal influenza prophylaxis in high-risk, elderly, and healthcare populations; Hepatitis B viral infection prevention in neonates, healthcare workers, and unimmunized adults
reference_dosage: Tetanus Toxoid: 0.5 ml IM; Rabies Vaccine post-exposure: 1.0 ml IM on Days 0, 3, 7, and 14–28 into deltoid muscle (NEVER gluteal).
common_side_effects: Injection site soreness, localized erythema, and mild swelling
Low-grade fever and malaise for 24–48 hours
serious_adverse_effects: Immediate severe anaphylaxis (laryngeal edema, bronchospasm, cardiovascular collapse)
Guillain-Barré Syndrome (extremely rare association)
Brachial neuritis or sterile injection abscess
contraindications: Severe immediate anaphylactic reaction to a previous dose of the same vaccine
Severe acute febrile illness (defer vaccination until fever resolves)
Live vaccines contraindicated in severe immunosuppression and pregnancy
drug_interactions: High-dose systemic immunosuppressive therapy and chemotherapy significantly impair protective antibody response
Rabies Immunoglobulin (RIG): Must infiltrate into and around wound edges; remaining volume IM at a site distant from vaccine
schedule: Schedule H Prescription Drug / Cold Chain Biological

approved_indications: Abnormal uterine bleeding (menorrhagia) and dysfunctional uterine bleeding; Luteal phase support in assisted reproductive technology (ART) and recurrent miscarriage prophylaxis; Endometriosis, secondary amenorrhea, and post-menopausal hormone therapy adjunct; Post-partum hemorrhage prevention and management (Tranexamic Acid / Oxytocin)

approved_indications: Secondary prevention of atherothrombotic events post-STEMI / NSTEMI / stroke; Non-valvular atrial fibrillation for systemic thromboembolism / stroke prevention; Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) treatment and prophylaxis; Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT)
reference_dosage: Ecosprin: 75–150 mg once daily post-meal; Clopidogrel: 75 mg once daily; Apixaban: 5 mg twice daily. Strictly per cardiology guidelines.
serious_adverse_effects: Major gastrointestinal bleeding
Intracranial hemorrhage and hemorrhagic stroke
Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT)
contraindications: Active pathological bleeding (peptic ulcer, intracranial bleed)
Severe thrombocytopenia (<50,000/uL)
Severe uncontrolled arterial hypertension (>180/110 mmHg)
drug_interactions: NSAIDs and Corticosteroids (substantially amplify GI ulceration and major bleeding risk)
CYP2C19 inhibitors (Omeprazole impairs Clopidogrel bioactivation; use Pantoprazole)
SSRIs (additive bleeding risk)

approved_indications: Impetigo, folliculitis, and secondary superficial bacterial skin infections; Tinea pedis (athlete's foot), tinea cruris (jock itch), and tinea corporis (ringworm); Acne vulgaris and inflammatory papulopustular lesions; Scabies infestation (Permethrin 5% lotion single application)
reference_dosage: Apply a thin film to the clean, dry affected area 2 to 3 times daily for 7–14 days. Avoid occlusive dressings unless directed.
serious_adverse_effects: Contact dermatitis and local skin sensitization
Cutaneous atrophy, telangiectasia, and striae with potent topical steroids (Clobetasol)
Systemic absorption and HPA suppression with extensive topical steroid use
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to active formulation or vehicle excipients
Viral skin lesions (herpes simplex, varicella) should not receive topical steroids
drug_interactions: Concomitant topical products on the same site may cause additive irritation or vehicle antagonism

approved_indications: Postmenopausal osteoporosis and senile osteoporosis with high fracture risk; Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis prevention and treatment; Paget's disease of bone; Symptomatic management of osteoarthritis and cartilage degeneration
reference_dosage: Alendronate: 70 mg once weekly; Ibandronate: 150 mg once monthly on the exact same date; Teriparatide: 20 mcg SC daily for up to 24 months.
common_side_effects: Musculoskeletal pain and mild joint stiffness
Transient flu-like symptoms after initial dose
serious_adverse_effects: Severe chemical ulcerative esophagitis and esophageal stricture if swallowed improperly or if lying down

Osteonecrosis of the jaw (ONJ) following invasive dental extractions

Inability to stand or sit upright for at least 30 minutes
Severe hypocalcemia (must correct prior to starting)
Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 35 mL/min)

NSAIDs worsen esophageal and gastric mucosal irritation

NSAIDs co-administered with Methotrexate dramatically elevate toxic blood levels
Allopurinol co-administered with Azathioprine requires 75% Azathioprine reduction to avoid fatal pancytopenia

approved_indications: Active immunization against Clostridium tetani following trauma or wound contamination; Post-exposure rabies prophylaxis following animal bites or scratches (WHO Category II & III); Annual seasonal influenza prophylaxis in high-risk, elderly, and healthcare populations; Hepatitis B viral infection prevention in neonates, healthcare workers, and unimmunized adults
reference_dosage: Tetanus Toxoid: 0.5 ml IM; Rabies Vaccine post-exposure: 1.0 ml IM on Days 0, 3, 7, and 14–28 into deltoid muscle (NEVER gluteal).
common_side_effects: Injection site soreness, localized erythema, and mild swelling
Low-grade fever and malaise for 24–48 hours
serious_adverse_effects: Immediate severe anaphylaxis (laryngeal edema, bronchospasm, cardiovascular collapse)
Guillain-Barré Syndrome (extremely rare association)
Brachial neuritis or sterile injection abscess
contraindications: Severe immediate anaphylactic reaction to a previous dose of the same vaccine
Severe acute febrile illness (defer vaccination until fever resolves)
Live vaccines contraindicated in severe immunosuppression and pregnancy
drug_interactions: High-dose systemic immunosuppressive therapy and chemotherapy significantly impair protective antibody response
Rabies Immunoglobulin (RIG): Must infiltrate into and around wound edges; remaining volume IM at a site distant from vaccine

approved_indications: Primary, secondary, and subclinical hypothyroidism (Hashimoto's thyroiditis, post-thyroidectomy); Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) suppression in differentiated thyroid cancer; Hyperthyroidism and Graves' disease (Carbimazole / Methimazole)
reference_dosage: Levothyroxine: Typical full replacement dose 1.6 mcg/kg/day (e.g., 50–100 mcg once daily). Titrate in 12.5–25 mcg increments every 6–8 weeks based on serum TSH.
common_side_effects: Usually absent at correct physiological replacement dose

drug_interactions: Beta-blockers: Prevent beta-2 bronchodilation, leading to unopposed alpha-mediated severe hypertension and reflex bradycardia (use Glucagon if refractory)

approved_indications: Severe acute bronchial asthma exacerbation and COPD status asthmaticus; Systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, and acute vasculitis flares; Severe allergic angioedema, anaphylaxis adjunctive therapy, and drug eruptions; Nephrotic syndrome and immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP)
reference_dosage: Prednisolone: 20–40 mg once daily morning for 5–7 days for acute asthma; taper gradually if treatment exceeds 2 weeks to avoid secondary adrenal crisis.
common_side_effects: Increased appetite and rapid weight gain
Fluid retention and facial mooning (Cushingoid features)
serious_adverse_effects: Secondary hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis suppression and adrenal crisis upon abrupt cessation
Hyperglycemia and steroid-induced diabetes
Opportunistic systemic infections and reactivation of latent tuberculosis
Avascular necrosis of the femoral head and severe osteoporosis
Posterior subcapsular cataracts and open-angle glaucoma
contraindications: Systemic untreated fungal or parasitic infections
Active untreated tuberculosis or viral infections (herpes simplex keratitis)
Concurrent live attenuated vaccines
drug_interactions: NSAIDs: Markedly increases risk of severe peptic ulceration and catastrophic GI bleeding
Antidiabetic medications: Corticosteroids elevate blood glucose, necessitating higher antidiabetic doses
Ketoconazole: Inhibits steroid metabolism, heightening toxicity

approved_indications: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus as monotherapy or combination pharmacotherapy; Cardiovascular and renal risk reduction in T2DM patients (SGLT-2 inhibitors); Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus and gestational diabetes (Insulin regimens)
reference_dosage: Metformin: 500 mg twice daily with meals, titrating up to 2,000 mg daily; Glimepiride: 1–2 mg once daily before breakfast.
serious_adverse_effects: Lactic acidosis (rare but fatal with Metformin in severe hypoxia/renal failure)
Severe neuroglycopenic hypoglycemia
Euglycemic Diabetic Ketoacidosis (SGLT-2i)
Acute pancreatitis (DPP-4i)
contraindications: Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min for Metformin/SGLT2i)
Acute metabolic acidosis, DKA, or diabetic coma
Severe hepatic failure
drug_interactions: Iodinated Radiocontrast agents (withhold Metformin 48h prior/after)
Systemic corticosteroids (antagonize glycemic control)
Beta-blockers (mask adrenergic hypoglycemia warning signs)

approved_indications: Infiltration anesthesia and peripheral nerve block for minor surgical and dental procedures; Surface topical anesthesia for endotracheal intubation, endoscopy, and urethral catheterization; Spinal and epidural anesthesia for obstetrical and lower abdominal / orthopedic surgery; Induction and maintenance of general anesthesia in procedural sedation (Propofol/Midazolam)
reference_dosage: Lignocaine 2% plain: Maximum single dose is 4.5 mg/kg body weight (not exceeding 300 mg); Lignocaine with adrenaline: Max 7 mg/kg (up to 500 mg). Strictly individualized.
common_side_effects: Mild localized burning or stinging during injection
Transient numbness and paresthesia in adjacent dermatomes
Mild hypotension upon spinal sympathetic blockade
serious_adverse_effects: Local Anesthetic Systemic Toxicity (LAST): Perioral numbness, metallic taste, auditory tinnitus, seizures, and cardiovascular collapse
Severe bupivacaine-induced refractory cardiac arrest and ventricular arrhythmias
Malignant hyperthermia and severe respiratory depression
contraindications: Severe cardiac conduction blocks (2nd or 3rd degree AV block without pacemaker)
Known hypersensitivity to amide-type local anesthetics
Injection into infected or acutely inflamed tissue (acidic pH prevents active drug penetration)
drug_interactions: Class I and III antiarrhythmics (additive cardiac electrophysiological depression)
Adrenaline-containing solutions MUST NOT be used for digital, penile, nasal, or ear-lobe block (causes severe ischemic necrosis)
schedule: Schedule H Prescription Drug / Controlled Hospital Anesthetic

approved_indications: Active immunization against Clostridium tetani following trauma or wound contamination; Post-exposure rabies prophylaxis following animal bites or scratches (WHO Category II & III); Annual seasonal influenza prophylaxis in high-risk, elderly, and healthcare populations; Hepatitis B viral infection prevention in neonates, healthcare workers, and unimmunized adults
reference_dosage: Tetanus Toxoid: 0.5 ml IM; Rabies Vaccine post-exposure: 1.0 ml IM on Days 0, 3, 7, and 14–28 into deltoid muscle (NEVER gluteal).
common_side_effects: Injection site soreness, localized erythema, and mild swelling
Low-grade fever and malaise for 24–48 hours
serious_adverse_effects: Immediate severe anaphylaxis (laryngeal edema, bronchospasm, cardiovascular collapse)
Guillain-Barré Syndrome (extremely rare association)
Brachial neuritis or sterile injection abscess
contraindications: Severe immediate anaphylactic reaction to a previous dose of the same vaccine
Severe acute febrile illness (defer vaccination until fever resolves)
Live vaccines contraindicated in severe immunosuppression and pregnancy
drug_interactions: High-dose systemic immunosuppressive therapy and chemotherapy significantly impair protective antibody response
Rabies Immunoglobulin (RIG): Must infiltrate into and around wound edges; remaining volume IM at a site distant from vaccine
schedule: Schedule H Prescription Drug / Cold Chain Biological

approved_indications: Primary, secondary, and subclinical hypothyroidism (Hashimoto's thyroiditis, post-thyroidectomy); Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) suppression in differentiated thyroid cancer; Hyperthyroidism and Graves' disease (Carbimazole / Methimazole)
reference_dosage: Levothyroxine: Typical full replacement dose 1.6 mcg/kg/day (e.g., 50–100 mcg once daily). Titrate in 12.5–25 mcg increments every 6–8 weeks based on serum TSH.
common_side_effects: Usually absent at correct physiological replacement dose
Signs of overtreatment: Palpitations, tachycardia, nervousness, heat intolerance, tremor, insomnia, weight loss
serious_adverse_effects: Cardiac arrhythmias (atrial fibrillation) and myocardial ischemia in elderly or ischemic heart disease patients
Accelerated bone mineral density loss and osteoporosis with chronic TSH suppression
Agranulocytosis with Carbimazole
contraindications: Uncorrected subclinical or overt thyrotoxicosis
Acute uncorrected adrenal insufficiency (may precipitate fatal adrenal crisis)
drug_interactions: Calcium, Iron, Calcium carbonate, Antacids, PPIs, Soy (severely impair Levothyroxine absorption; separate by 4 hours)
Warfarin (Levothyroxine potentiates anticoagulant effect)

approved_indications: Primary, secondary, and subclinical hypothyroidism (Hashimoto's thyroiditis, post-thyroidectomy); Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) suppression in differentiated thyroid cancer; Hyperthyroidism and Graves' disease (Carbimazole / Methimazole)
reference_dosage: Levothyroxine: Typical full replacement dose 1.6 mcg/kg/day (e.g., 50–100 mcg once daily). Titrate in 12.5–25 mcg increments every 6–8 weeks based on serum TSH.
common_side_effects: Usually absent at correct physiological replacement dose
Signs of overtreatment: Palpitations, tachycardia, nervousness, heat intolerance, tremor, insomnia, weight loss
serious_adverse_effects: Cardiac arrhythmias (atrial fibrillation) and myocardial ischemia in elderly or ischemic heart disease patients
Accelerated bone mineral density loss and osteoporosis with chronic TSH suppression
Agranulocytosis with Carbimazole
contraindications: Uncorrected subclinical or overt thyrotoxicosis
Acute uncorrected adrenal insufficiency (may precipitate fatal adrenal crisis)
drug_interactions: Calcium, Iron, Calcium carbonate, Antacids, PPIs, Soy (severely impair Levothyroxine absorption; separate by 4 hours)
Warfarin (Levothyroxine potentiates anticoagulant effect)

approved_indications: Primary, secondary, and subclinical hypothyroidism (Hashimoto's thyroiditis, post-thyroidectomy); Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) suppression in differentiated thyroid cancer; Hyperthyroidism and Graves' disease (Carbimazole / Methimazole)
reference_dosage: Levothyroxine: Typical full replacement dose 1.6 mcg/kg/day (e.g., 50–100 mcg once daily). Titrate in 12.5–25 mcg increments every 6–8 weeks based on serum TSH.
common_side_effects: Usually absent at correct physiological replacement dose
Signs of overtreatment: Palpitations, tachycardia, nervousness, heat intolerance, tremor, insomnia, weight loss
serious_adverse_effects: Cardiac arrhythmias (atrial fibrillation) and myocardial ischemia in elderly or ischemic heart disease patients
Accelerated bone mineral density loss and osteoporosis with chronic TSH suppression
Agranulocytosis with Carbimazole
contraindications: Uncorrected subclinical or overt thyrotoxicosis
Acute uncorrected adrenal insufficiency (may precipitate fatal adrenal crisis)
drug_interactions: Calcium, Iron, Calcium carbonate, Antacids, PPIs, Soy (severely impair Levothyroxine absorption; separate by 4 hours)
Warfarin (Levothyroxine potentiates anticoagulant effect)

approved_indications: Pyrexia (fever) secondary to infectious, inflammatory, or post-vaccination etiology; Mild-to-moderate somatic pain (headache, tension headache, migraine attack); Musculoskeletal discomfort, backache, arthralgia, and dental pain; Primary dysmenorrhea and post-procedural discomfort
reference_dosage: Adults: 500 mg–650 mg orally every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Maximum daily dose MUST NOT exceed 4,000 mg (4g) in 24 hours.
serious_adverse_effects: Dose-dependent acute hepatic necrosis (N-acetyl-p-benzoquinone imine hepatotoxicity)
Renal tubular necrosis
Thrombocytopenia or leukopenia
contraindications: Severe active hepatic impairment or acute viral hepatitis
Documented hypersensitivity to paracetamol
drug_interactions: Chronic heavy alcohol intake markedly potentiates hepatotoxic risk
Warfarin: Regular high doses (>2g/day) may elevate INR
Isoniazid (elevates hepatotoxic metabolite formation)

approved_indications: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus as monotherapy or combination pharmacotherapy; Cardiovascular and renal risk reduction in T2DM patients (SGLT-2 inhibitors); Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus and gestational diabetes (Insulin regimens)
reference_dosage: Metformin: 500 mg twice daily with meals, titrating up to 2,000 mg daily; Glimepiride: 1–2 mg once daily before breakfast.
serious_adverse_effects: Lactic acidosis (rare but fatal with Metformin in severe hypoxia/renal failure)
Severe neuroglycopenic hypoglycemia
Euglycemic Diabetic Ketoacidosis (SGLT-2i)
Acute pancreatitis (DPP-4i)
contraindications: Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min for Metformin/SGLT2i)
Acute metabolic acidosis, DKA, or diabetic coma
Severe hepatic failure
drug_interactions: Iodinated Radiocontrast agents (withhold Metformin 48h prior/after)
Systemic corticosteroids (antagonize glycemic control)
Beta-blockers (mask adrenergic hypoglycemia warning signs)

approved_indications: Vitamin D deficiency, nutritional rickets, and osteomalacia / osteoporosis prophylaxis; Peripheral neuropathy, diabetic neuropathy, and vitamin B12 deficiency anemia; Iron deficiency anemia and nutritional prophylaxis during pregnancy and lactation; Neural tube defect prevention (Preconceptional Folic Acid supplementation)
reference_dosage: Cholecalciferol: 60,000 IU once weekly for 8 weeks, followed by once monthly maintenance; Calcium: 500–1000 mg daily post-meals; Methylcobalamin: 1500 mcg daily.
common_side_effects: Constipation, dark tarry stools, and nausea (Iron supplements)
serious_adverse_effects: Hypercalcemia, metastatic tissue calcification, and renal calculi (Vitamin D / Calcium toxicity)
Iron overload / hemochromatosis in non-iron deficiency states
contraindications: Hypercalcemia, hypervitaminosis D, or severe nephrolithiasis
Hemochromatosis, hemosiderosis, or active hemolytic anemia (for iron supplements)
drug_interactions: Iron and Calcium bind and inactivate Fluoroquinolones and Tetracyclines (separate by 2–3 hours)
Thiazide diuretics increase hypercalcemia risk when co-administered with high-dose calcium/vitamin D

approved_indications: Secondary prevention of atherothrombotic events post-STEMI / NSTEMI / stroke; Non-valvular atrial fibrillation for systemic thromboembolism / stroke prevention; Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) treatment and prophylaxis; Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT)
reference_dosage: Ecosprin: 75–150 mg once daily post-meal; Clopidogrel: 75 mg once daily; Apixaban: 5 mg twice daily. Strictly per cardiology guidelines.
serious_adverse_effects: Major gastrointestinal bleeding
Intracranial hemorrhage and hemorrhagic stroke
Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT)
contraindications: Active pathological bleeding (peptic ulcer, intracranial bleed)
Severe thrombocytopenia (<50,000/uL)
Severe uncontrolled arterial hypertension (>180/110 mmHg)
drug_interactions: NSAIDs and Corticosteroids (substantially amplify GI ulceration and major bleeding risk)
CYP2C19 inhibitors (Omeprazole impairs Clopidogrel bioactivation; use Pantoprazole)
SSRIs (additive bleeding risk)

approved_indications: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and erosive esophagitis; Peptic and duodenal ulcer healing and maintenance therapy; Zollinger-Ellison syndrome and gastric hypersecretory states; NSAID-associated mucosal ulcer prophylaxis and H. pylori eradication protocols
reference_dosage: Adults: 40 mg orally once daily 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast for 4–8 weeks. Intravenous: 40 mg IV slow bolus.
serious_adverse_effects: Long-term hypomagnesemia and vitamin B12 malabsorption
Increased incidence of Clostridioides difficile colitis
Elevated risk of osteoporotic hip fractures with multi-year high-dose therapy
Acute interstitial nephritis
contraindications: Known severe hypersensitivity to pantoprazole, substituted benzimidazoles, or excipients
drug_interactions: Clopidogrel: Some PPIs (omeprazole) may reduce antiplatelet bioactivation; prefer pantoprazole
Iron supplements, Ketoconazole (reduced bioavailability due to elevated gastric pH)
Methotrexate (PPIs may delay clearance, increasing toxicity)

approved_indications: Essential systemic hypertension in adults; Cardiovascular risk reduction in diabetic and coronary artery disease patients; Stable chronic angina pectoris and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction; Diabetic nephropathy with microalbuminuria
reference_dosage: Telmisartan: 40–80 mg once daily; Amlodipine: 5–10 mg once daily; Metoprolol: 25–50 mg twice daily. Titrate according to clinical BP targets.
serious_adverse_effects: Symptomatic hypotension and syncope
Hyperkalemia (ARBs, ACEi, Spironolactone)
Severe bradycardia or heart block (Beta-blockers)
Angioedema
contraindications: Pregnancy (ARBs & ACE inhibitors carry fatal fetotoxicity warning)
Bilateral renal artery stenosis
Severe cardiogenic shock or 2nd/3rd degree AV block (Beta-blockers)
drug_interactions: Potassium supplements/Potassium-sparing diuretics (severe hyperkalemia risk)
NSAIDs (blunt BP reduction and increase renal failure risk)
Phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors (excessive hypotension)
